text: HDFC Large Cap Fund: minimum SIP shown on the official scheme page is ₹100. The page labels the scheme risk as Very High. It states an exit load of 1.00% for redemptions or switch-outs within 1 year from allotment; no exit load after 1 year. The page also lists the benchmark as Nifty 100 TRI.

HDFC Large Cap Fund official page provides links to the SID, KIM, leaflet and fund facts document. Its TER is displayed on the scheme page and can change over time, so the assistant should cite the current official page rather than hard-code a historical value.

HDFC Flexi Cap Fund: the official page describes it as an open-ended equity mutual fund investing across large-cap, mid-cap and small-cap stocks. Minimum SIP shown is ₹100. Risk label shown is Very High. Exit load is 1.00% if redeemed or switched out within 1 year from allotment; no exit load after 1 year. Benchmark shown is NIFTY 500 Total Returns Index.

HDFC ELSS Tax Saver: minimum SIP shown on the official scheme page is ₹500. Exit load shown is NIL. The scheme is an ELSS and has a statutory 3-year lock-in from the date of allotment of the respective units.

HDFC ELSS Tax Saver official presentation states: lock-in period is 3 years from the date of allotment of the respective units; entry load and exit load are nil; benchmark is NIFTY 500 Total Returns Index.

HDFC Balanced Advantage Fund: official page shows minimum SIP of ₹100 and risk label Very High. Up to 15% of units from each purchase/switch-in may be redeemed without exit load; redemption above that limit is subject to 1.00% exit load if within 1 year from allotment and no exit load after 1 year.

HDFC Mutual Fund's Download Statement page says an Account Statement is a consolidated document summarizing mutual-fund transactions such as purchases, redemptions, switches, dividends and units allotted. It states that there is no charge for receiving or downloading the account statement.

HDFC Mutual Fund's Request Statement page provides routes for account statement, dividend statement, exit-load statement, capital-gains statement, consolidated account statement and consolidated realized gains statement.

HDFC Mutual Fund's capital-gain statement guide explains that capital-gain statements summarize realized gains and losses for a selected period and describes obtaining statements through RTAs, platforms and AMC websites. The assistant should not request PAN, email, phone, OTP or other personal identifiers.

HDFC Mutual Fund's SIP FAQ explains that exit load is a predetermined percentage applicable when investments are redeemed before the specified time, and that the exact load depends on the fund's applicable rules.
SEBI Investor defines exit load as a fee charged by a mutual fund when units are redeemed before a predefined period. Different schemes can have different exit-load structures.
SEBI Investor explains that the Riskometer is used to depict the risk level associated with a mutual-fund scheme and provides standardized risk categories from Low through Very High.

AMFI explains that investors can obtain a consolidated account statement (CAS) showing holdings across mutual funds through e-CAS services from CAMS and KFintech, and can also use MF Central to view/download portfolio and CAS.

AMFI explains that a mutual-fund factsheet typically includes scheme name, investment objective, scheme type, fund manager, AUM, NAV, load information, benchmark, expense ratio and portfolio information.
AMFI's Investor Corner provides educational resources on mutual funds, including expense ratio, risks, scheme categorization, SIP and other investor topics.
AMFI provides scheme-wise disclosure pages for mutual-fund investment disclosures in accordance with SEBI requirements.
